findings.description: Danziger et al. (2011) 'hungry judges' study cited as established fact without disclosing the replication controversy. Glöckner (2016) demonstrated the pattern could reflect case-ordering effects rather than resource depletion. The study remains widely cited but contested; presenting it as settled evidence misrepresents its epistemic status.
findings.suggestion: Hedge with 'Danziger and colleagues (2011) reported' and add an epistemic note: 'Though this specific finding faces replication scrutiny (Glöckner, 2016), the broader SDT principle — that depleted reasoners shift toward conservative defaults — holds across multiple paradigms.' Alternatively, replace with a less contested citation for cognitive-load effects on decision criteria.
findings.context: Kahneman (1973) established that cognitive resources deplete under sustained work. Danziger and colleagues (2011) documented the behavioral consequence in judicial decisions: judges granted parole more frequently at session start and after breaks, then shifted toward denial as the session lengthened.

findings.description: Post lacks an EPISTEMIC FLAGS section. The companion icescr-sixtieth-anniversary post includes a well-formed EPISTEMIC FLAGS block documenting five claims requiring verification. This SDT post makes specific empirical claims (contested Danziger study, specific SDT parameter claims) and references unpublished calibration data — without any epistemic flag disclosure.
findings.suggestion: Add an EPISTEMIC FLAGS section before the footer. Minimum flags: (1) Danziger 2011 replication status; (2) the 0.30 cognitive reserve threshold is a working convention in A2A-Psychology, not an empirically derived value; (3) the claim that 'activation patterns produce empirical estimates of d-prime' assumes the activation data collection infrastructure exists and calibrates correctly.
findings.context: File ends at line 81 with transport footer. No EPISTEMIC FLAGS section present. Reference: icescr post has flags at lines 81-88.

findings.description: Summary metadata states 'The worst conditions for economic rights since the Cold War split' as absolute fact. The post body appropriately hedges comparable claims (e.g., the 'permission structure' inference is flagged as analytical). The summary — which surfaces as SEO metadata and social previews — presents a stronger claim than the body supports. The EPISTEMIC FLAGS section does not flag this comparative claim.
findings.suggestion: Soften to 'conditions that researchers describe as among the most serious since the Cold War' or flag the comparative claim ('most serious since...') in the EPISTEMIC FLAGS section with the basis for the comparison.
findings.context: summary: 'The worst conditions for economic rights since the Cold War split.'

findings.description: White House citation links to the fact-sheets directory (`https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/`) rather than a specific document. Readers cannot verify the sixty-six organizations withdrawal claim from this link. The directory may contain hundreds of fact sheets and the specific January 20, 2026 document requires additional navigation.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a direct link to the specific White House fact sheet (if archived) or note the document title so readers can locate it. If the specific URL has been taken down (as administration websites sometimes delete prior fact sheets), note 'archived at [Wayback Machine URL]' or cite via an established news organization that quoted the original document.

findings.description: Cross-post internal link hardcodes the production domain (`https://blog.unratified.org/posts/2026-04-20-apophatic-agent-psychology/`). Other posts in this series use relative paths. The hardcoded URL breaks in development and staging environments and diverges from the site's internal linking convention.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a relative path: `/posts/2026-04-20-apophatic-agent-psychology/` — consistent with how the icescr series footer links its prior posts.

findings.description: Core SDT terminology ('d-prime', 'criterion' in the decision-threshold sense) appears throughout the post but absent from the glossary. The glossary covers discriminator, differential-diagnosis, and related methodology terms — but Signal Detection Theory vocabulary falls outside current glossary coverage. Readers unfamiliar with psychophysics lack a canonical reference point.
findings.suggestion: Add glossary entries for: 'd-prime' (discriminability measure separating signal from noise distributions in SDT), 'criterion' (decision threshold — the evidence level an observer requires before choosing signal), and optionally 'SDT' as an abbreviation entry pointing to both. Category: 'methodology' fits existing taxonomy.
findings.context: A discriminability measure (d-prime) captures the system's fundamental ability to distinguish signal from noise. A criterion parameter captures where the system places its decision threshold
